## What

`artifacts/backlog/README.md` opens with:

```text
<!-- GENERATED FILE - do not edit by hand. Re-run the backlog script after changing anything in items/. -->
```

and states that item frontmatter is the source of truth and *"this page is derived from it"*. There
is no such script. `package.json` exposes only `npm test`; a repository search for the generated
progress phrasing returns the README and nothing that produces it. The derivation exists as a human
procedure.

## Why

This is EP-06's property applied to the backlog itself. The tracker reports counts and percentages
as though computed, and nothing establishes that they were. A stale hand-edited number is
indistinguishable from a derived one, on the surface [IN-01](./IN-01.md) treats as this project's
authoritative liveness record.

Recorded now rather than earlier because there is a concrete specimen instead of a worry. Adding
[ST-08](./ST-08.md) and [ST-09](./ST-09.md) in `c45a4e4` required hand-editing **five** separate
derived figures — the leaf ratio and its percentage, the progress bar, the status table's
not-started count and total, the hierarchy table's story count, and the theme row's done/remaining —
plus the tree. Each was an opportunity to be quietly wrong, and the only check available was
arithmetic performed by the same party that wrote the numbers.

## Notes

**Stated narrowly on purpose.** This is not "build a backlog system", and not necessarily "write a
generator". The acceptance property:

> Given the item files, there is one deterministic way to reproduce or check the tracker, such that
> a stale hand-edited count cannot remain green.

A checker that recomputes and fails on disagreement satisfies it as well as a generator does, and is
the smaller change. Whichever is chosen, the header must end up telling the truth: either the file is
generated by something runnable, or it stops claiming to be.

The precedent for preferring a check over a second producer is already in this family of
repositories — `scripts/inventory.mjs` in FinancialStandards compares rather than derives, so the
two copies cannot silently disagree.

## Closed 2026-08-16

A checker, as the acceptance property allowed. `scripts/backlog.mjs` recomputes every mechanical
claim on the tracker from item frontmatter; `test/backlog-tracker.test.mjs` runs it under `npm test`,
which is what `ci/checks.sh` executes on both the container and the hosted runner. The header no
longer claims to be generated, and a test asserts that it does not.

Evidence: [2026-08-16-backlog-derivation.md](../../evidence/2026-08-16-backlog-derivation.md).

**The acceptance property, met exactly.** There is now one deterministic way to check the tracker,
and a stale hand-edited count cannot remain green. Closing this item was the first thing the checker
policed: it moved nine derived figures, and named all nine.

**The claim is bounded to what is derived.** Nine figures are computed and compared — the leaf ratio
and bar, four status counts and the total, six type counts, the theme row, the in-flight list, the
ready list, and every tree line including each parent tuple. Prose on the page is not checked and is
not claimed to be. Nothing here validates that the *hierarchy* is well-shaped beyond parent
existence, reachability, prefix agreement and the closed-date pairing; the level-skip
[ST-09](./ST-09.md) records is still unvalidated, deliberately.

**Why the mutations matter more than the check.** Neutering the tree and list comparison leaves the
primary check green while seven mutations go red. A reconciliation script that agrees with today's
numbers is not evidence that a wrong number would be caught, and that gap is precisely the shape of
the defect this item was filed against.
